LESSON: LINES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: GEOMETRY Strand Sub- strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experi
Topic 3.1: Lines
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Lines, part of GEOMETRY Strand Sub- strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning Experi in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do you make a line?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign words related to lines for learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify straight lines in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. draw straight lines on different surfaces,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. identify curved lines in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. draw curved lines on different surfaces,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Lines in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. observe lines in different objects from the environment. ● Learners in pairs or groups are guided to fingerspell and sign words related to lines such as straight lines, curved lines, circle and semi-circle. ● Learners in pairs or groups are guided to stand behind/ besides each other facing the same side and identify what they have formed as a straight line. ● Learners in pairs or groups are guided to mark two points on the ground and use a stick/a string to join the two points to make a straight line. ● Learners in pairs or groups are guided to practise drawing straight lines on the ground and in their books. ● Learners in groups to form a semi-circle and one of them to draw a line around it and identify the semi- circle drawn as a curved line. ● Learners in groups to practise drawing curved lines on the charts and attach them in their portfolio. ● Learners in groups are guided to look and identify lines from different objects in the environment. How do you make a line? 25 Core Competence to be developed: ● Learning to learn: Develop relationships as learners works with peers to draw a straight line. ● Self-efficacy: learner recognises straight and curved lines from real objects in the environment

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Lines together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity: Cooperation by working together to form lines.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness as learners maintains cleanliness and order as they form lines.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of drawing lines to the concept of Drawing in Creative Activities. .
